original_question: Let w be a multilinear commutator word, and assume that G is a group where the set of w-values is covered by finitely many cyclic subgroups. Is it true that the verbal subgroup w(G) is finite-by-cyclic? This is true for lower central words(G. Cutolo, C. Nicotera, J. Algebra, 324, no. 7(2010), 1616–1624).
target_in_paper: Problem 21.98 (New Problems, 21st Issue, 2026) of The Kourovka Notebook.
correct_elements: Your draft already tracks the official problem almost verbatim: it has the correct class of words (multilinear commutator words), the correct ambient setting (an arbitrary group G, not specifically finite or profinite), the correct hypothesis (the set of all w-values is contained in a finite union of cyclic subgroups), the correct subgroup under study (the verbal subgroup w(G)), and the correct conclusion to test (whether w(G) is finite-by-cyclic). It also retains the same motivating solved special case mentioned in the paper, namely the lower central words.
missing_details: To be fully stand-alone, define a multilinear commutator word as a commutator of weight n in n distinct variables.
Explicitly define the set of w-values as G_w = {w(g1,...,gn) : g1,...,gn ∈ G}.
Explicitly define the verbal subgroup as w(G) = ⟨G_w⟩, the subgroup generated by all w-values.
Spell out finite-by-cyclic as: there exists a finite normal subgroup N of w(G) such that w(G)/N is cyclic.

State explicitly that the covering cyclic subgroups are subgroups of G and that the problem is purely existential; no quantitative bound in terms of the number of covering subgroups is part of the official formulation.
refined_question: Let w = w(x1,...,xn) be a multilinear commutator word, that is, a commutator of weight n in n distinct variables. For a group G, let G_w = {w(g1,...,gn) : g1,...,gn ∈ G} be the set of w-values, and let w(G) = ⟨G_w⟩ be the corresponding verbal subgroup. Suppose there exist finitely many cyclic subgroups C1,...,Cm ≤ G such that G_w ⊆ C1 ∪ ... ∪ Cm. Must there exist a finite normal subgroup N ◁ w(G) such that w(G)/N is cyclic?
justification: The draft is already very close to the official formulation. In the cited arXiv paper, the exact target is Problem 21.98, which asks precisely whether, for a multilinear commutator word w and a group G whose w-values are covered by finitely many cyclic subgroups, the verbal subgroup w(G) must be finite-by-cyclic. The only additions needed to make the question fully stand-alone are definitional: the notebook separately supplies the meaning of “multilinear commutator word,” and elsewhere in the same volume it makes explicit that a verbal subgroup is the subgroup generated by the set of word-values. The lower-central-word remark is part of Problem 21.98 itself, so your draft is already paper-faithful and only needs those explicit definitions.
